name: Advanced Micro Devices
key_signal: AMD's price has stalled just below its 50-day SMA (495.76 vs 499.08) with a negative MACD histogram and RSI near 46, signaling short-term momentum exhaustion after a +122% six-month run.
thesis: AMD remains structurally strong: revenue growth of 37.8% and earnings growth of 91% reflect accelerating AI GPU/MI300-series adoption, gross margins over 53%, and a golden cross with price still 67% above the 200-day SMA confirm the primary uptrend is intact. Forward PE of 36.8x is demanding but not absurd for a company compounding earnings at this rate, and 47 analysts rate it strong buy, reflecting broad institutional conviction in the AI infrastructure buildout narrative that has driven the stock from $149 to near $500 over the past year.
bear_case: The technical picture shows genuine fatigue — 21-day momentum has turned negative (-2.3%), MACD histogram is deeply negative (-7.9), and price has slipped below its 50-day moving average after a parabolic 122% six-month advance, which is exactly the setup that precedes multi-month consolidation or a sharper drawdown, especially with 30-day annualized volatility above 82% and beta of 2.47 amplifying any market-wide risk-off move. Fundamentally, trailing PE of 164x and price-to-book of 12.5x price in years of flawless execution, while ROE of just 8% and debt-to-equity of 6.0x reveal a balance sheet and profitability profile that doesn't yet justify the multiple if AI capex growth decelerates or Nvidia/hyperscaler custom silicon competition erodes AMD's data-center GPU share gains — with 47 analysts already at strong buy, most of the good news is arguably already priced in, leaving asymmetric downside risk to any guidance disappointment.
